theorem lt_antisymm {s₁ s₂ : String} (h₁ : ¬s₁ < s₂) (h₂ : ¬s₂ < s₁) : s₁ = s₂ := by
  simp at h₁ h₂
20→  exact String.le_antisymm h₂ h₁

  .compareOfLessAndEq_of_irrefl_of_trans_of_antisymm

30→private theorem add_utf8Size_pos : 0 < i + Char.utf8Size c :=
  Nat.add_pos_right _ (Char.utf8Size_pos c)

private theorem ne_add_utf8Size_add_self : i ≠ n + Char.utf8Size c + i :=
  Nat.ne_of_lt (Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left add_utf8Size_pos)

private theorem ne_self_add_add_utf8Size : i ≠ i + (n + Char.utf8Size c) :=
  Nat.ne_of_lt (Nat.lt_add_of_pos_right add_utf8Size_pos)

/-- The UTF-8 byte length of a list of characters. (This is intended for specification purposes.) -/
40→@[inline] def utf8Len : List Char → Nat := utf8ByteSize.go

@[simp] theorem utf8ByteSize.go_eq : utf8ByteSize.go = utf8Len := rfl

@[simp] theorem utf8ByteSize_mk (cs) : utf8ByteSize ⟨cs⟩ = utf8Len cs := rfl

@[simp] theorem utf8Len_nil : utf8Len [] = 0 := rfl

@[simp] theorem utf8Len_cons (c cs) : utf8Len (c :: cs) = utf8Len cs + c.utf8Size := rfl

50→@[simp] theorem utf8Len_append (cs₁ cs₂) : utf8Len (cs₁ ++ cs₂) = utf8Len cs₁ + utf8Len cs₂ := by
  induction cs₁ <;> simp [*, Nat.add_right_comm]

theorem utf8Len_reverseAux (cs₁ cs₂) :
    utf8Len (cs₁.reverseAux cs₂) = utf8Len cs₁ + utf8Len cs₂ := by
  induction cs₁ generalizing cs₂ <;> simp_all [← Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_right_comm]

@[simp] theorem utf8Len_reverse (cs) : utf8Len cs.reverse = utf8Len cs := utf8Len_reverseAux ..

@[simp] theorem utf8Len_eq_zero : utf8Len l = 0 ↔ l = [] := by
60→  cases l <;> simp [Nat.ne_zero_iff_zero_lt.mpr (Char.utf8Size_pos _)]

open List
theorem utf8Len_le_of_sublist : ∀ {cs₁ cs₂}, cs₁ <+ cs₂ → utf8Len cs₁ ≤ utf8Len cs₂
  | _, _, .slnil => Nat.le_refl _
  | _, _, .cons _ h => Nat.le_trans (utf8Len_le_of_sublist h) (Nat.le_add_right ..)
  | _, _, .cons₂ _ h => Nat.add_le_add_right (utf8Len_le_of_sublist h) _

theorem utf8Len_le_of_infix (h : cs₁ <:+: cs₂) : utf8Len cs₁ ≤ utf8Len cs₂ :=
70→  utf8Len_le_of_sublist h.sublist

theorem utf8Len_le_of_suffix (h : cs₁ <:+ cs₂) : utf8Len cs₁ ≤ utf8Len cs₂ :=
  utf8Len_le_of_sublist h.sublist

theorem utf8Len_le_of_prefix (h : cs₁ <+: cs₂) : utf8Len cs₁ ≤ utf8Len cs₂ :=
  utf8Len_le_of_sublist h.sublist
end

private theorem zero_ne_addChar {i : Pos} {c : Char} : 0 ≠ i + c :=
  ne_of_lt add_utf8Size_pos

/-- A string position is valid if it is equal to the UTF-8 length of an initial substring of `s`. -/
def Valid (s : String) (p : Pos) : Prop :=
  ∃ cs cs', cs ++ cs' = s.1 ∧ p.1 = utf8Len cs

@[simp] theorem valid_zero : Valid s 0 := ⟨[], s.1, rfl, rfl⟩

theorem Valid.mk (cs cs' : List Char) : Valid ⟨cs ++ cs'⟩ ⟨utf8Len cs⟩ := ⟨cs, cs', rfl, rfl⟩

/-- The UTF-8 byte length of a list of characters. (This is intended for specification purposes.) -/

def Valid (s : String) (p : Pos) : Prop :=

/--
Induction along the valid positions in a list of characters.
(This definition is intended only for specification purposes.)
-/
def utf8InductionOn {motive : List Char → Pos → Sort u}
    (s : List Char) (i p : Pos)
    (nil : ∀ i, motive [] i)
    (eq  : ∀ c cs, motive (c :: cs) p)
    (ind : ∀ (c : Char) cs i, i ≠ p → motive cs (i + c) → motive (c :: cs) i) :
    motive s i :=
  match s with
  | [] => nil i
  | c::cs =>
    if h : i = p then
      h ▸ eq c cs
    else ind c cs i h (utf8InductionOn cs (i + c) p nil eq ind)

import Std

def isSafeChar (c : Char) : Bool :=
  ('a' ≤ c && c ≤ 'z') ||
  ('A' ≤ c && c ≤ 'Z') ||
  ('0' ≤ c && c ≤ '9') ||
  c == '_' || c == '@' || c == '%' || c == '+' || c == '=' ||
  c == ':' || c == ',' || c == '.' || c == '/' || c == '-'

def quoteEscape : String := "'\"'\"'"

def escapeChar (c : Char) : String :=
  if c == '\'' then quoteEscape else String.singleton c

def escapeQuotes (s : String) : String :=
  String.join (s.data.map escapeChar)

def quote (s : String) : String :=
  if s.data.isEmpty then
    "''"
  else if s.data.all isSafeChar then
    s
  else
    "'" ++ escapeQuotes s ++ "'"

def quoteImp (s : String) : String :=
  Id.run do
    if s.data.isEmpty then
      return "''"
    let mut allSafe : Bool := true
    for c in s.data do
      if isSafeChar c = false then
        allSafe := false
    if allSafe then
      return s
    let mut acc : List Char := ['\'']
    for c in s.data do
      if c == '\'' then
        acc := acc ++ quoteEscape.data
      else
        acc := acc.push c
    acc := acc.push '\''
    return String.mk acc

#eval quote ""
#eval quote "abc"
#eval quote "a b c"
#eval quote "a'b"
#eval quote "'"
#eval quote "a'b" == "'a'\"'\"'b'"
#eval quoteImp "a'b"
#eval quoteImp "a b c"
#eval quoteImp ""
#eval quoteImp "abc"
#eval quoteImp "'"

example : quote "" = "''" := by native_decide
example : quote "abc" = "abc" := by native_decide
example : quote "a b c" = "'a b c'" := by native_decide
example : quote "a'b" = "'a'\"'\"'b'" := by native_decide
example : isSafeChar '\'' = false := by decide
example : isSafeChar 'a' = true := by decide
example : isSafeChar ' ' = false := by decide
example : isSafeChar '-' = true := by decide
example : isSafeChar '/' = true := by decide
example : isSafeChar '_' = true := by decide

-- try a small proof
theorem safe_not_quote (c : Char) (h : isSafeChar c = true) : c ≠ '\'' := by
  intro heq
  subst heq
  simp [isSafeChar] at h

/--
We can express a for loop over a list as a fold,
in which whenever we reach `.done b` we keep that value through the rest of the fold.
-/
theorem forIn_eq_foldlM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    {l : List α} (f : α → β → m (ForInStep β)) (init : β) :
    forIn l init f = ForInStep.value <$>
380→      l.foldlM (fun b a => match b with
        | .yield b => f a b
        | .done b => pure (.done b)) (ForInStep.yield init) := by
  induction l generalizing init with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a as ih =>
    simp only [foldlM_cons, forIn_cons, _root_.map_bind]
    congr 1
    funext x
    match x with
390→    | .done b =>
      clear ih
      dsimp
      induction as with
      | nil => simp
      | cons a as ih => simp [ih]
    | .yield b =>
      simp [ih]

/-- We can express a for loop over a list which always yields as a fold. -/
400→@[simp] theorem forIn_yield_eq_foldlM [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    {l : List α} (f : α → β → m γ) (g : α → β → γ → β) (init : β) :
    forIn l init (fun a b => (fun c => .yield (g a b c)) <$> f a b) =
      l.foldlM (fun b a => g a b <$> f a b) init := by
  simp only [forIn_eq_foldlM]
  induction l generalizing init <;> simp_all

@[simp] theorem forIn_pure_yield_eq_foldl [Monad m] [LawfulMonad m]
    {l : List α} (f : α → β → β) (init : β) :
    forIn l init (fun a b => pure (.yield (f a b))) =
410→      pure (f := m) (l.foldl (fun b a => f a b) init) := by
  simp only [forIn_eq_foldlM]
  induction l generalizing init <;> simp_all

@[simp] theorem idRun_forIn_yield_eq_foldl
    (l : List α) (f : α → β → Id β) (init : β) :
    (forIn l init (fun a b => .yield <$> f a b)).run =
      l.foldl (fun b a => f a b |>.run) init :=

def isSafeChar (c : Char) : Bool :=
  ('a' ≤ c && c ≤ 'z') ||
  ('A' ≤ c && c ≤ 'Z') ||
  ('0' ≤ c && c ≤ '9') ||
  c == '_' || c == '@' || c == '%' || c == '+' || c == '=' ||
  c == ':' || c == ',' || c == '.' || c == '/' || c == '-'

def quoteEscape : String := "'\"'\"'"

def escapeChar (c : Char) : String :=
  if c == '\'' then quoteEscape else String.singleton c

def escapeQuotes (s : String) : String :=
  String.join (s.data.map escapeChar)

def quote (s : String) : String :=
  if s.data.isEmpty then
    "''"
  else if s.data.all isSafeChar then
    s

import Lean.Elab.Tactic.Config
import Plausible.Sampleable


10→/-!
# `Testable` Class

Testable propositions have a procedure that can generate counter-examples
together with a proof that they invalidate the proposition.

This is a port of the Haskell QuickCheck library.

## Creating Customized Instances

20→The type classes `Testable`, `SampleableExt` and `Shrinkable` are the
means by which `Plausible` creates samples and tests them. For instance,
the proposition `∀ i j : Nat, i ≤ j` has a `Testable` instance because `Nat`
is sampleable and `i ≤ j` is decidable. Once `Plausible` finds the `Testable`
instance, it can start using the instance to repeatedly creating samples
and checking whether they satisfy the property. Once it has found a
counter-example it will then use a `Shrinkable` instance to reduce the
example. This allows the user to create new instances and apply
`Plausible` to new situations.

30→### What do I do if I'm testing a property about my newly defined type?

Let us consider a type made for a new formalization:

```lean
structure MyType where
  x : Nat
  y : Nat
  h : x ≤ y
  deriving Repr
40→```

How do we test a property about `MyType`? For instance, let us consider
`Testable.check <| ∀ a b : MyType, a.y ≤ b.x → a.x ≤ b.y`. Writing this
property as is will give us an error because we do not have an instance
of `Shrinkable MyType` and `SampleableExt MyType`. We can define one as follows:

```lean
instance : Shrinkable MyType where
  shrink := fun ⟨x, y, _⟩ =>
50→    let proxy := Shrinkable.shrink (x, y - x)
    proxy.map (fun (fst, snd) => ⟨fst, fst + snd, by omega⟩)

instance : SampleableExt MyType :=
  SampleableExt.mkSelfContained do
    let x ← SampleableExt.interpSample Nat
    let xyDiff ← SampleableExt.interpSample Nat
    return ⟨x, x + xyDiff, by omega⟩
```

60→Again, we take advantage of the fact that other types have useful
`Shrinkable` implementations, in this case `Prod`.

## Main definitions

* `Testable` class
* `Testable.check`: a way to test a proposition using random examples

## References

70→* https://hackage.haskell.org/package/QuickCheck

-/

namespace Plausible

/-- Result of trying to disprove `p` -/

10→/-!
# `Testable` Class

Testable propositions have a procedure that can generate counter-examples
together with a proof that they invalidate the proposition.

This is a port of the Haskell QuickCheck library.

## Creating Customized Instances

20→The type classes `Testable`, `SampleableExt` and `Shrinkable` are the
means by which `Plausible` creates samples and tests them. For instance,
the proposition `∀ i j : Nat, i ≤ j` has a `Testable` instance because `Nat`
is sampleable and `i ≤ j` is decidable. Once `Plausible` finds the `Testable`
instance, it can start using the instance to repeatedly creating samples
and checking whether they satisfy the property. Once it has found a
counter-example it will then use a `Shrinkable` instance to reduce the
example. This allows the user to create new instances and apply
`Plausible` to new situations.

30→### What do I do if I'm testing a property about my newly defined type?

Let us consider a type made for a new formalization:

```lean
structure MyType where
  x : Nat
  y : Nat
  h : x ≤ y
  deriving Repr
40→```

How do we test a property about `MyType`? For instance, let us consider
`Testable.check <| ∀ a b : MyType, a.y ≤ b.x → a.x ≤ b.y`. Writing this
property as is will give us an error because we do not have an instance
of `Shrinkable MyType` and `SampleableExt MyType`. We can define one as follows:

```lean
instance : Shrinkable MyType where
  shrink := fun ⟨x, y, _⟩ =>
50→    let proxy := Shrinkable.shrink (x, y - x)
    proxy.map (fun (fst, snd) => ⟨fst, fst + snd, by omega⟩)

instance : SampleableExt MyType :=
  SampleableExt.mkSelfContained do
    let x ← SampleableExt.interpSample Nat
    let xyDiff ← SampleableExt.interpSample Nat
    return ⟨x, x + xyDiff, by omega⟩
```

60→Again, we take advantage of the fact that other types have useful
`Shrinkable` implementations, in this case `Prod`.

## Main definitions

* `Testable` class
* `Testable.check`: a way to test a proposition using random examples

160→variable {p q : Prop}

instance (priority := low) : PrintableProp p where
  printProp := "⋯"

/-- `Testable p` uses random examples to try to disprove `p`. -/
class Testable (p : Prop) where
  run (cfg : Configuration) (minimize : Bool) : Gen (TestResult p)

def NamedBinder (_n : String) (p : Prop) : Prop := p
170→
namespace TestResult

def toString : TestResult p → String
  | success (PSum.inl _) => "success (no proof)"
  | success (PSum.inr _) => "success (proof)"
  | gaveUp n => s!"gave {n} times"
  | failure _ counters _ => s!"failed {counters}"

instance : ToString (TestResult p) := ⟨toString⟩
180→
/-- Applicative combinator proof carrying test results. -/
def combine {p q : Prop} : Unit ⊕' (p → q) → Unit ⊕' p → Unit ⊕' q
  | PSum.inr f, PSum.inr proof => PSum.inr <| f proof
  | _, _ => PSum.inl ()

/-- Combine the test result for properties `p` and `q` to create a test for their conjunction. -/
def and : TestResult p → TestResult q → TestResult (p ∧ q)
  | failure h xs n, _ => failure (fun h2 => h h2.left) xs n
  | _, failure h xs n => failure (fun h2 => h h2.right) xs n
190→  | success h1, success h2 => success <| combine (combine (PSum.inr And.intro) h1) h2
  | gaveUp n, gaveUp m => gaveUp <| n + m
  | gaveUp n, _ => gaveUp n
  | _, gaveUp n => gaveUp n

/-- Combine the test result for properties `p` and `q` to create a test for their disjunction. -/
def or : TestResult p → TestResult q → TestResult (p ∨ q)
  | failure h1 xs n, failure h2 ys m =>
    let h3 := fun h =>
      match h with
200→      | Or.inl h3 => h1 h3
      | Or.inr h3 => h2 h3
    failure h3 (xs ++ ys) (n + m)
  | success h, _ => success <| combine (PSum.inr Or.inl) h
  | _, success h => success <| combine (PSum.inr Or.inr) h
  | gaveUp n, gaveUp m => gaveUp <| n + m
  | gaveUp n, _ => gaveUp n
  | _, gaveUp n => gaveUp n

/-- If `q → p`, then `¬ p → ¬ q` which means that testing `p` can allow us
210→to find counter-examples to `q`. -/
def imp (h : q → p) (r : TestResult p)
    (p : Unit ⊕' (p → q) := PSum.inl ()) : TestResult q :=
  match r with
  | failure h2 xs n => failure (mt h h2) xs n
  | success h2 => success <| combine p h2
  | gaveUp n => gaveUp n

/-- Test `q` by testing `p` and proving the equivalence between the two. -/
def iff (h : q ↔ p) (r : TestResult p) : TestResult q :=
220→  imp h.mp r (PSum.inr h.mpr)

/-- When we assign a value to a universally quantified variable,
we record that value using this function so that our counter-examples
can be informative. -/
def addInfo (x : String) (h : q → p) (r : TestResult p)
    (p : Unit ⊕' (p → q) := PSum.inl ()) : TestResult q :=
  if let failure h2 xs n := r then
    failure (mt h h2) (x :: xs) n
  else
230→    imp h r p

/-- Add some formatting to the information recorded by `addInfo`. -/
def addVarInfo {γ : Type _} [Repr γ] (var : String) (x : γ) (h : q → p) (r : TestResult p)
    (p : Unit ⊕' (p → q) := PSum.inl ()) : TestResult q :=
  addInfo s!"{var} := {repr x}" h r p

def isFailure : TestResult p → Bool
  | failure _ _ _ => true
  | _ => false
240→
end TestResult

namespace Configuration

/-- A configuration with all the trace options enabled, useful for debugging. -/
def verbose : Configuration where
  traceDiscarded := true
  traceSuccesses := true
  traceShrink := true
250→  traceShrinkCandidates := true

end Configuration

namespace Testable

open TestResult

def runProp (p : Prop) [Testable p] : Configuration → Bool → Gen (TestResult p) := Testable.run

/-- `DecorationsOf p` is used as a hint to `mk_decorations` to specify
that the goal should be satisfied with a proposition equivalent to `p`
with added annotations. -/
abbrev DecorationsOf (_p : Prop) := Prop

open Elab.Tactic
open Meta

/-- In a goal of the shape `⊢ DecorationsOf p`, `mk_decoration` examines
570→the syntax of `p` and adds `NamedBinder` around universal quantifications
to improve error messages. This tool can be used in the declaration of a
function as follows:
```lean
def foo (p : Prop) (p' : Decorations.DecorationsOf p := by mk_decorations) [Testable p'] : ...
```
`p` is the parameter given by the user, `p'` is a definitionally equivalent
proposition where the quantifiers are annotated with `NamedBinder`.
-/
scoped elab "mk_decorations" : tactic => do
580→  let goal ← getMainGoal
  let goalType ← goal.getType
  if let .app (.const ``Decorations.DecorationsOf _) body := goalType then
    closeMainGoal `mk_decorations (← addDecorations body)

end Decorations

open Decorations in
/-- Run a test suite for `p` and throw an exception if `p` does not hold. -/
def Testable.check (p : Prop) (cfg : Configuration := {})
590→    (p' : Decorations.DecorationsOf p := by mk_decorations) [Testable p'] : Lean.CoreM PUnit := do
  match ← Testable.checkIO p' cfg with
  | TestResult.success _ => if !cfg.quiet then Lean.logInfo "Unable to find a counter-example"
  | TestResult.gaveUp n =>
    if !cfg.quiet then
      let msg := s!"Gave up after failing to generate values that fulfill the preconditions {n} times."
      Lean.logWarning msg
  | TestResult.failure _ xs n =>
    let msg := "Found a counter-example!"
    if cfg.quiet then
600→      Lean.throwError msg
    else
      Lean.throwError <| formatFailure msg xs n

--   Configuration.verbose
-- #eval Testable.check (∀ (x : Nat) (h : 10 < x), 5 < x) Configuration.verbose

def slimTrace {m : Type → Type _} [Pure m] (s : String) : m PUnit :=
  dbgTrace s!"[Plausible: {s}]" (fun _ => pure ())

instance andTestable [Testable p] [Testable q] : Testable (p ∧ q) where
  run := fun cfg min => do
    let xp ← runProp p cfg min
    let xq ← runProp q cfg min
    return and xp xq

270→instance orTestable [Testable p] [Testable q] : Testable (p ∨ q) where
  run := fun cfg min => do
    let xp ← runProp p cfg min
    -- As a little performance optimization we can just not run the second
    -- test if the first succeeds
    match xp with
    | success (PSum.inl h) => return success (PSum.inl h)
    | success (PSum.inr h) => return success (PSum.inr <| Or.inl h)
    | _ =>
      let xq ← runProp q cfg min
280→      return or xp xq

instance iffTestable [Testable ((p ∧ q) ∨ (¬ p ∧ ¬ q))] : Testable (p ↔ q) where
  run := fun cfg min => do
    let h ← runProp ((p ∧ q) ∨ (¬ p ∧ ¬ q)) cfg min
    have := by
      constructor
      · intro h
        simp [h, Classical.em]
      · intro h
290→        rcases h with ⟨hleft, hright⟩ | ⟨hleft, hright⟩ <;> simp [hleft, hright]
    return iff this h

variable {var : String}

instance decGuardTestable [PrintableProp p] [Decidable p] {β : p → Prop} [∀ h, Testable (β h)] :
    Testable (NamedBinder var <| ∀ h, β h) where
  run := fun cfg min => do
    if h : p then
      let res := runProp (β h) cfg min
300→      let s := printProp p
      (fun r => addInfo s!"guard: {s}" (· <| h) r (PSum.inr <| fun q _ => q)) <$> res
    else if cfg.traceDiscarded || cfg.traceSuccesses then
      let res := fun _ => return gaveUp 1
      let s := printProp p
      slimTrace s!"discard: Guard {s} does not hold"; res
    else
      return gaveUp 1

310→    Testable (NamedBinder var <| ∀ x, f x) where
  run := fun cfg min => do
    let r ← runProp (f Int) cfg min
    return addVarInfo var "Int" (· <| Int) r

/--
Format the counter-examples found in a test failure.
-/
def formatFailure (s : String) (xs : List String) (n : Nat) : String :=
  let counter := String.intercalate "\n" xs
  let parts := [
    "\n===================",
330→    s,
    counter,
    s!"({n} shrinks)",
    "-------------------"
  ]
  String.intercalate "\n" parts

/--
Increase the number of shrinking steps in a test result.
-/
340→def addShrinks (n : Nat) : TestResult p → TestResult p
  | TestResult.failure p xs m => TestResult.failure p xs (m + n)
  | p => p

universe u in
instance {α : Type u} {m : Type u → Type _} [Pure m] : Inhabited (OptionT m α) :=
  ⟨(pure none : m (Option α))⟩

variable {α : Sort _}

350→/-- Shrink a counter-example `x` by using `Shrinkable.shrink x`, picking the first
candidate that falsifies a property and recursively shrinking that one.
The process is guaranteed to terminate because `shrink x` produces
a proof that all the values it produces are smaller (according to `SizeOf`)
than `x`. -/
partial def minimizeAux [SampleableExt α] {β : α → Prop} [∀ x, Testable (β x)] (cfg : Configuration)
    (var : String) (x : SampleableExt.proxy α) (n : Nat) :
    OptionT Gen (Σ x, TestResult (β (SampleableExt.interp x))) := do
  let candidates := SampleableExt.shrink.shrink x
  if cfg.traceShrinkCandidates then
360→    slimTrace s!"Candidates for {var} := {repr x}:\n  {repr candidates}"
  for candidate in candidates do
    if cfg.traceShrinkCandidates then
      slimTrace s!"Trying {var} := {repr candidate}"
    let res ← OptionT.lift <| Testable.runProp (β (SampleableExt.interp candidate)) cfg true
    if res.isFailure then
      if cfg.traceShrink then
        slimTrace s!"{var} shrunk to {repr candidate} from {repr x}"
      let currentStep := OptionT.lift <| return Sigma.mk candidate (addShrinks (n + 1) res)
      let nextStep := minimizeAux cfg var candidate (n + 1)
370→      return ← (nextStep <|> currentStep)
  if cfg.traceShrink then
    slimTrace s!"No shrinking possible for {var} := {repr x}"
  failure

/-- Once a property fails to hold on an example, look for smaller counter-examples
to show the user. -/
def minimize [SampleableExt α] {β : α → Prop} [∀ x, Testable (β x)] (cfg : Configuration)
    (var : String) (x : SampleableExt.proxy α) (r : TestResult (β <| SampleableExt.interp x)) :
    Gen (Σ x, TestResult (β <| SampleableExt.interp x)) := do
380→  if cfg.traceShrink then
     slimTrace "Shrink"
     slimTrace s!"Attempting to shrink {var} := {repr x}"
  let res ← OptionT.run <| minimizeAux cfg var x 0
  return res.getD ⟨x, r⟩

/-- Test a universal property by creating a sample of the right type and instantiating the
bound variable with it. -/
instance varTestable [SampleableExt α] {β : α → Prop} [∀ x, Testable (β x)] :
    Testable (NamedBinder var <| ∀ x : α, β x) where
390→  run := fun cfg min => do
    let x ← SampleableExt.sample
    if cfg.traceSuccesses || cfg.traceDiscarded then
      slimTrace s!"{var} := {repr x}"
    let r ← Testable.runProp (β <| SampleableExt.interp x) cfg false
    let ⟨finalX, finalR⟩ ←
      if isFailure r then
        if cfg.traceSuccesses then
          slimTrace s!"{var} := {repr x} is a failure"
        if min then
400→          minimize cfg var x r
        else
          pure ⟨x, r⟩
      else
        pure ⟨x, r⟩
    return addVarInfo var finalX (· <| SampleableExt.interp finalX) finalR

/-- Test a universal property about propositions -/
instance propVarTestable {β : Prop → Prop} [∀ b : Bool, Testable (β b)] :
  Testable (NamedBinder var <| ∀ p : Prop, β p)
410→where
  run := fun cfg min =>
    imp (fun h (b : Bool) => h b) <$> Testable.runProp (NamedBinder var <| ∀ b : Bool, β b) cfg min

instance (priority := high) unusedVarTestable {β : Prop} [Nonempty α] [Testable β] :
  Testable (NamedBinder var (α → β))
where
  run := fun cfg min => do
    if cfg.traceDiscarded || cfg.traceSuccesses then
      slimTrace s!"{var} is unused"
420→    let r ← Testable.runProp β cfg min
    let finalR := addInfo s!"{var} is irrelevant (unused)" id r
    return imp (· <| Classical.ofNonempty) finalR (PSum.inr <| fun x _ => x)

instance (priority := 2000) subtypeVarTestable {p : α → Prop} {β : α → Prop}
    [∀ x, PrintableProp (p x)]
    [∀ x, Testable (β x)]
    [SampleableExt (Subtype p)] {var'} :
    Testable (NamedBinder var <| (x : α) → NamedBinder var' <| p x → β x) where
  run cfg min :=
430→    letI (x : Subtype p) : Testable (β x) :=
      { run := fun cfg min => do
          let r ← Testable.runProp (β x.val) cfg min
          return addInfo s!"guard: {printProp (p x)} (by construction)" id r (PSum.inr id) }
    do
      let r ← @Testable.run (∀ x : Subtype p, β x.val) (@varTestable var _ _ _ _) cfg min
      have := by simp [Subtype.forall, NamedBinder]
      return iff this r

instance (priority := low) decidableTestable {p : Prop} [PrintableProp p] [Decidable p] :
440→    Testable p where
  run := fun _ _ =>
    if h : p then
      return success (PSum.inr h)
    else
      let s := printProp p
      return failure h [s!"issue: {s} does not hold"] 0

end Testable

instance Eq.printableProp [Repr α] {x y : α} : PrintableProp (x = y) where
  printProp := s!"{repr x} = {repr y}"

instance Ne.printableProp [Repr α] {x y : α} : PrintableProp (x ≠ y) where
  printProp := s!"{repr x} ≠ {repr y}"

@[simp]
theorem length_flatMap {l : List α} {f : α → List β} :
    length (l.flatMap f) = sum (map (fun a => (f a).length) l) := by
  rw [List.flatMap, length_flatten, map_map, Function.comp_def]

@[simp, grind] theorem mem_flatMap {f : α → List β} {b} {l : List α} : b ∈ l.flatMap f ↔ ∃ a, a ∈ l ∧ b ∈ f a := by
  simp [flatMap_def, mem_flatten]
  exact ⟨fun ⟨_, ⟨a, h₁, rfl⟩, h₂⟩ => ⟨a, h₁, h₂⟩, fun ⟨a, h₁, h₂⟩ => ⟨_, ⟨a, h₁, rfl⟩, h₂⟩⟩

theorem exists_of_mem_flatMap {b : β} {l : List α} {f : α → List β} :
    b ∈ l.flatMap f → ∃ a, a ∈ l ∧ b ∈ f a := mem_flatMap.1

  n < 0xd800 ∨ (0xdfff < n ∧ n < 0x110000)

20→namespace Char

One character is less than another if its code point is strictly less than the other's.
-/
@[expose] protected def lt (a b : Char) : Prop := a.val < b.val

One character is less than or equal to another if its code point is less than or equal to the
other's.
30→-/
@[expose] protected def le (a b : Char) : Prop := a.val ≤ b.val

instance : LE Char := ⟨Char.le⟩

  UInt32.decLt _ _

def isSafeChar (c : Char) : Bool :=
  (decide ('a' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'z')) ||
  (decide ('A' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'Z')) ||
  (decide ('0' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ '9')) ||
  (c == '_') || (c == '@') || (c == '%') || (c == '+') || (c == '=') ||
  (c == ':') || (c == ',') || (c == '.') || (c == '/') || (c == '-')

def escapedQuoteData : List Char := ['\'', '"', '\'', '"', '\'']

def escapedQuote : String := ⟨escapedQuoteData⟩

def escapeOne (c : Char) : List Char :=
  if c == '\'' then escapedQuoteData else [c]

def escapeQuotes (s : String) : String :=
  ⟨s.data.flatMap escapeOne⟩

def quote (s : String) : String :=
  let cs := s.data
  if cs.isEmpty then
    "''"
  else if cs.all isSafeChar then
    s
  else
    "'" ++ escapeQuotes s ++ "'"

def quoteImp (s : String) : String :=
  Id.run do
    if s.data.isEmpty then
      return "''"
    let mut allSafe : Bool := true
    for c in s.data do
      if isSafeChar c = false then
        allSafe := false
    if allSafe then
      return s
    let mut acc : List Char := ['\'']
    for c in s.data do
      if c == '\'' then
        acc := acc ++ quoteEscapeData
      else
        acc := acc ++ [c]
    acc := acc ++ ['\'']
    return String.mk acc
  where
    quoteEscapeData := escapedQuoteData

theorem isSafeChar_quote : isSafeChar '\'' = false := by decide

theorem isSafeChar_iff (c : Char) :
    isSafeChar c = true ↔
      ('a' ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 'z') ∨ ('A' ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 'Z') ∨ ('0' ≤ c ∧ c ≤ '9') ∨
      c = '_' ∨ c = '@' ∨ c = '%' ∨ c = '+' ∨ c = '=' ∨
      c = ':' ∨ c = ',' ∨ c = '.' ∨ c = '/' ∨ c = '-' := by
  simp only [isSafeChar, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, beq_iff_eq]

theorem forIn_safe_loop (cs : List Char) (b : Bool) :
    (forIn cs b fun c r =>
      if isSafeChar c = false then ForInStep.yield false else ForInStep.yield r)
    = (b && cs.all isSafeChar) := by
  induction cs generalizing b with
  | nil => simp [List.forIn_nil, Bool.and_true]
  | cons c cs ih =>
    simp only [List.forIn_cons, List.all_cons, bind, pure, Id.run]
    by_cases h : isSafeChar c = false
    · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, ih, Bool.and_false]
    · have ht : isSafeChar c = true := by cases hc : isSafeChar c <;> grind
      simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, ih, ht, Bool.true_and]

    (forIn cs acc fun c r =>
      if (c == '\'') = true then ForInStep.yield (r ++ escapedQuoteData)
      else ForInStep.yield (r ++ [c]))
    = acc ++ cs.flatMap escapeOne := by
  induction cs generalizing acc with
  | nil => simp [List.forIn_nil, List.append_nil]
  | cons c cs ih =>
    simp only [List.forIn_cons, List.flatMap_cons, bind, pure, escapeOne]
    by_cases h : (c == '\'') = true
    · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, ih, List.append_assoc]
    · simp only [h, ↓reduceIte, ih, List.append_assoc]

theorem data_two_quotes : ("''" : String).data = ['\'', '\''] := by decide

theorem escapedQuote_literal : escapedQuote = "'\"'\"'" := by decide

  simp only [quote, quoteImp, quoteImp.quoteEscapeData, Id.run, bind, pure, escapeQuotes]
  have hsafe := forIn_safe_loop s.data true
  simp only [hsafe, Bool.true_and] at *
  have hesc := forIn_escape_loop s.data ['\'']
  simp only [hesc]
  split
  · rfl
  · split
    · rfl
    · apply String.ext
      simp [String.data_append, data_single_quote]

  | [] => some []
  | c :: cs =>
      if c == '\'' then
        match cs with
        | '"' :: '\'' :: '"' :: '\'' :: rest =>
            (List.cons '\'') <$> unescape rest
        | _ => none
      else
        (List.cons c) <$> unescape cs

    unescape (cs.flatMap escapeOne) = some cs := by
  induction cs with
  | nil => simp [unescape]

      if rest.getLast? == some '\'' then

      else
        none
  | _ => none

  simp [stripQuotes, List.getLast?_concat, List.dropLast_concat]

    some ⟨cs⟩

  | mk _ => rfl

        s.data
      else
        ['\''] ++ s.data.flatMap escapeOne ++ ['\''] := by

  split
  · simp [data_two_quotes]
  · split

    · simp [String.data_append, data_single_quote]

  refine List.all_eq_false.mpr ?_
  refine ⟨'\'', ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp
  · simpa [isSafeChar_quote]

  rw [quote_data]

  | nil => simp
  | cons c cs ih =>

  cases s with
  | mk _ => rfl

def isSafeChar (c : Char) : Bool :=
  (decide ('a' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'z')) ||

    (forIn (m := Id) cs b fun c r =>
        (if p c = false then ForInStep.yield false else ForInStep.yield r)) =

        cases hp : p c <;> simp_all

def escapedQuoteData : List Char := ['\'', '"', '\'', '"', '\'']

def escapeOne (c : Char) : List Char :=
  if (c == '\'') = true then escapedQuoteData else [c]

theorem forIn_safe_loop (cs : List Char) (b : Bool) (p : Char → Bool) :
    (forIn (m := Id) cs b fun c r =>
        match p c with
        | true => ForInStep.yield r
        | false => ForInStep.yield false) =
      (b && cs.all p) := by
  induction cs generalizing b with
  | nil =>
    simp only [List.forIn_nil, List.all_nil, Bool.and_true, pure]
  | cons c cs ih =>
    rw [List.forIn_cons, List.all_cons]
    cases hp : p c with
    | false =>
      simp only [hp, Bind.bind, ih, Bool.false_and, Bool.and_false]
    | true =>
      simp only [hp, Bind.bind, ih, Bool.true_and]

theorem forIn_escape_loop (cs acc : List Char) (step : Char → List Char) :
    (forIn (m := Id) cs acc fun c r => ForInStep.yield (r ++ step c)) =
      acc ++ cs.flatMap step := by
  induction cs generalizing acc with
  | nil =>
    simp only [List.forIn_nil, pure, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil]
  | cons c cs ih =>
    rw [List.forIn_cons, List.flatMap_cons]
    simp only [Bind.bind, ih, List.append_assoc]

def isSafeChar (c : Char) : Bool :=
  (decide ('a' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'z')) ||
  (decide ('A' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'Z')) ||
  (decide ('0' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ '9')) ||
  (c == '_') || (c == '@') || (c == '%') || (c == '+') || (c == '=') ||
  (c == ':') || (c == ',') || (c == '.') || (c == '/') || (c == '-')

def quote (s : String) : String :=
  if s.data.isEmpty = true then
    "''"
  else if s.data.all isSafeChar = true then
    s
  else
    "'" ++ ⟨s.data.flatMap escapeOne⟩ ++ "'"

def quoteImp (s : String) : String :=
  Id.run do
    if s.data.isEmpty = true then
      return "''"
    let mut allSafe : Bool := true
    for c in s.data do
      match isSafeChar c with
      | true => allSafe := allSafe
      | false => allSafe := false
    if allSafe = true then
      return s
    let mut acc : List Char := ['\'']
    for c in s.data do
      acc := acc ++ escapeOne c
    acc := acc ++ ['\'']
    return String.mk acc

  have hesc := forIn_escape_loop s.data ['\''] escapeOne

  split
  · rfl
  · split
    · rfl
    · apply String.ext
      simp [String.data_append]
      decide

def isSafeChar (c : Char) : Bool :=
  (decide ('a' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'z')) ||
  (decide ('A' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ 'Z')) ||
  (decide ('0' ≤ c) && decide (c ≤ '9')) ||
  (c == '_') || (c == '@') || (c == '%') || (c == '+') || (c == '=') ||
  (c == ':') || (c == ',') || (c == '.') || (c == '/') || (c == '-')

def escapedQuoteData : List Char := ['\'', '"', '\'', '"', '\'']

def escapeOne (c : Char) : List Char :=
  cond (c == '\'') escapedQuoteData [c]

def quoteList (cs : List Char) : List Char :=
  cond cs.isEmpty ['\'', '\'']
    (cond (cs.all isSafeChar) cs (['\''] ++ cs.flatMap escapeOne ++ ['\'']))

def quote (s : String) : String :=
  if s.data.isEmpty = true then
    "''"
  else if s.data.all isSafeChar = true then
    s
  else
    "'" ++ ⟨s.data.flatMap escapeOne⟩ ++ "'"

def unescape : List Char → Option (List Char)
  | [] => some []
  | c :: cs =>
      cond (c == '\'')
        (match cs with
          | '"' :: '\'' :: '"' :: '\'' :: rest =>
              Option.map (List.cons '\'') (unescape rest)
          | _ => none)
        (Option.map (List.cons c) (unescape cs))

theorem unescape_quote (rest : List Char) :
    unescape (escapedQuoteData ++ rest) = Option.map (List.cons '\'') (unescape rest) := by
  rfl

theorem unescape_other (c : Char) (rest : List Char) (h : (c == '\'') = false) :
    unescape (c :: rest) = Option.map (List.cons c) (unescape rest) := by
  conv =>
    lhs
    unfold unescape
  rw [h, cond_false]

theorem unescape_escape (cs : List Char) :
    unescape (cs.flatMap escapeOne) = some cs := by
  induction cs with
  | nil => simp [List.flatMap_nil, unescape]
  | cons c cs ih =>
    rw [List.flatMap_cons]
    cases h : (c == '\'') with
    | true =>
        rw [escapeOne, h, cond_true, unescape_quote, ih, Option.map_some]
        have hc : c = '\'' := by simpa [beq_iff_eq] using h
        simp [hc]
    | false =>
        rw [escapeOne, h, cond_false, List.singleton_append, unescape_other c _ h, ih,
          Option.map_some]

  | [] => none
  | c :: rest =>
      if (c == '\'') = false then
        none
      else if rest.getLast? == some '\'' then
        some rest.dropLast
      else
        none

    stripQuotes ('\'' :: (body ++ ['\''])) = some body := by
  simp only [stripQuotes, List.getLast?_concat, List.dropLast_concat]
  rfl

theorem all_wrap_false (body : List Char) :

  have h : ['\''] ++ body ++ ['\''] = '\'' :: (body ++ ['\'']) := rfl
  simp only [h, List.all_cons, isSafeChar_quote, Bool.false_and]
